extracted.intended_audience: writers, literary critics, and educated readers interested in aesthetics and criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive/aesthetic guidance about producing and evaluating literature and art, focusing on the critic's role, the nature of language, rhythm, unity, and the relation between creation and criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical faculty as essential to creation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Without the critical faculty, there is no artistic creation at all, worthy of the name."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text argues that the act of selection, judgment, and taste (the critical faculty) is not separate from but constitutive of fine artistic creation. The 'spirit of choice' and 'tact of omission' are presented as the same faculty functioning in creation. Anti-pattern: treating criticism as merely derivative or secondary to creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice and the ear as the ultimate test of writing
rubrics_metrics.description: "Their test was always the spoken word in its musical and metrical relations. The voice was the medium, and the ear the critic."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate prose and poetry by how they sound when spoken: rhythm, musicality, metrical movement. The essay criticises a tendency since printing to appeal more to the eye than to the ear. Example/anti-pattern: prose that resembles 'a piece of mosaic' (visual design) rather than music, which 'seems... to lack the true rhythmical life of words.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-consciousness and deliberateness of great imaginative work
rubrics_metrics.description: "All fine imaginative work is self-conscious and deliberate. No poet sings because he must sing... A great poet sings because he chooses to sing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great art is the product of conscious craft and choice, not merely spontaneous or unconscious impulse. Evaluation should reward evidence of deliberate shaping and control rather than claims of effortless inspiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity and style are necessary conditions of art
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is no art where there is no style, and no style where there is no unity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess works for coherent individual style and unity of effect; these qualities mark a work as 'made' rather than merely accidental or collective. Anti-pattern: works that feel fragmentary or lacking an author's individual imprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature's unique capacity to realise movement and temporal development
rubrics_metrics.description: "Movement, that problem of the visible arts, can be truly realised by Literature alone."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge literature on its ability to represent growth, the passage of time, change in characters and events—qualities that visual arts (statue, painting) cannot fully accomplish. Preference for narratives that show sequences, ageing, and development rather than frozen instants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language as the primary material of art and object of criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: "Words have not merely music... colour... and plastic form... thought and passion and spirituality are theirs also... If the Greeks had criticised nothing but language, they would still have been the great art-critics of the world."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism should attend closely to the material of language—its rhythm, sonic qualities, diction, and syntactic movements—analysing prose metrically as a musician analyses harmony and counterpoint. Scoring attention to diction and musical movement in sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism should analyse impression and its source (Aristotelian method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aristotle 'sets himself to analyse that impression, to investigate its source, to see how it is engendered.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good critique explains how a work produces its emotional or aesthetic effect (e.g., κάθαρσις in tragedy), examining plot, language, and presentation to show the mechanics of the impression. Scoring guidance: favour analyses that trace cause-effect between technique and felt response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism is itself a creative, independent art
rubrics_metrics.description: "Criticism is no more to be judged by any low standard of imitation or resemblance than is the work of poet or sculptor... Criticism is, in fact, both creative and independent."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate criticism by its own artistic and intellectual merits rather than by how well it mirrors or summarizes the criticized work. A critic may use humble subjects and still produce 'flawless' work—judge on style, insight, and imaginative power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection, tact of omission, and the 'spirit of choice' as a core skill
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'spirit of choice, that subtle tact of omission, is really the critical faculty in one of its most characteristic moods.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess creators by their ability to omit, distill, and select what is essential—recognising that omission and restraint are creative strengths. Anti-pattern: overproduction of irrelevant detail or failure to pare material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation arises from criticism, not mere creative instinct
rubrics_metrics.description: "The mere creative instinct does not innovate, but reproduces. It is to the critical instinct that we owe each new school...the critical faculty invents fresh forms."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value works that demonstrate informed formal experimentation shaped by critical reflection. Creativity without the guiding scrutiny of a critical sensibility tends to repetition; innovation should be credited where there is evident critical reworking of form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer cultivation and maintaining standards
rubrics_metrics.description: "Criticism demands infinitely more cultivation than creation does... The difficulty that I should fancy the reviewer feels is the difficulty of sustaining any standard."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors/reviewers should be highly cultivated, able to sustain standards rather than drifting to faddish judgments. Anti-patterns: indiscriminate praise or vulgar sensationalism; critics reduced to 'reporters of the police-court of literature.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical reviewing guideline: quick formal judgement by instinct
rubrics_metrics.description: "Ten minutes are really sufficient, if one has the instinct for form. Who wants to wade through a dull volume? One tastes it, and that is quite enough—more than enough..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For practical reviewing, the essay endorses rapid assessment focused on form and instinct for structure rather than exhaustive reading. Caveat: this presumes a cultivated instinct; misuse leads to superficial judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critic can elevate trivial materials by treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: "He does not even require for the perfection of his art the finest materials. Anything will serve his purpose... from subjects of little or of no importance... the true critic can... produce work that will be flawless in beauty and instinct with intellectual subtlety."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating critical or creative work, give weight to treatment and form over the inherent grandeur of subject-matter. A small or domestic subject can be exemplary if handled with consummate craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess tragic art by its purifying effect (κάθαρσις)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aristotle's conception: tragedy 'purifies the bosom of much
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tragedy should be evaluated on how it engenders pity and awe and effects a purification or spiritualising of the spectator; successful tragic art produces a lasting ethical/aesthetic effect rather than mere moralising.
